name: losses of the year

attributes.attribute: a divination rite of Scotland and Ireland
read at Samhain whether the year will be light or heavy

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Losses of the year is a ritual of Scotland and Ireland. At Samhain, the feast that closes one year and opens the next on the first of November, the folk played games of divination. They sought to learn what was called the losses of the year. The rite asked if the coming months would bring few troubles or many. In Scotland the rite moved to the New Year. The house was cleaned and swept of the bad of the past, and a first guest read the luck of the year to come.

okr.objective: Record the rite that reads the losses of the year.
key_results: The rite is a game of divination at Samhain.
It asks what the coming year will hold in store.
In Scotland the custom moved to the New Year.
